title: Control Plane handoff synthesis — weekly compaction
content:
TL;DR: Short, noisy week. Two partial degradations surfaced (kv cache misses + incorrect route affinity), small auth token storm due to renewed cert rollout, quotas scheduler hit a regression in steady-state fairness. No customer-facing outages, impact limited to increased p95 latency for internal batch jobs and quota rejections on some low-tier customers.

Attendees: Maya T., Diego M., Sana A., Liam O'C, Priya R. (SRE), Ezra V. (serving-runtime on-call) — ad-hoc: product observability drop-in.

Agenda:
- Quick pulse + metrics snapshot
- Incident/near-miss review (2 items)
- Rolling changes and canary progress (allocator + auth caching)
- Quota scheduler regression follow-up + mitigation plan
- Action items & owners

Pulse / Metrics (this week vs last):
- Median control-plane route decision latency: 8ms -> 9.2ms (↑15%)
- p95 control-plane: 28ms -> 48ms during two spikes (kv-cache miss storm)
- Auth token validation error rate: 0.02% -> 0.4% for 18 minutes (during cert rotate)
- Quota rejection rate (low tier): 0.1% -> 0.9% sustained for 2 hours before auto-fallback engaged
- Canary success: allocator experiment (k=3) small-scale looks fine; throttling back while we confirm fairness metrics

Incident summaries (brief):
1) KV cache miss storm — 2027-08-03 09:14–09:32 UTC
   - Symptom: sudden spike in route decision latency and p95 token runtime up across 3 clusters.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): small race in prefix cache invalidation + concurrent rehydration under high write traffic caused many requests to miss the fast-path and fall through to slower lookup.
   - Mitigation applied: temporary increase of background rehydration workers + capped rehydration concurrency (rollout within 15m).
   - Follow-ups: add stronger invariants around cache invalidation; instrument rehydration queue depth and time-to-hotload.

2) Auth token storm during cert rotate — 2027-08-04 02:07–02:25 UTC
   - Symptom: auth service saw bursts of token validation failures, leading to transient rejects for token-intact requests because of an asymmetric cache warm path.
   - Root cause: cert rotation changed token issuer metadata ordering; edge sidecars requested revalidation en masse instead of incrementally.
   - Mitigation: short-term hotfix that throttles validation refresh to 200 req/s per region; also rolled micro-delay back to token refresher (PR #412).
   - Follow-ups: prefer fast-path signing-key fingerprinting over full metadata fetch; add canary for cert rotations that simulates sidecar refresh load.

Quota scheduler regression (follow-up):
- Symptoms: low-tier accounts saw higher-than-expected rejections when overall cluster load was moderate.
- Root cause: change in fairness heuristic introduced in RATE-198 inadvertently prioritized recently active tenants, starving low-burst ones.
- Immediate mitigation: revert heuristic in prod for 2 clusters and enable legacy fairness for low-tier orgs.
- Next steps: refine the heuristic, add synthetic workload tests to reproduce the starvation pattern, and add a SLA-based fallback that ensures minimum baseline tokens for tenants.

Rolling changes + experiments status:
- Allocator fallback experiment (k=3) — canary at 3% traffic. Observed ~2% increase in short-tail latency for certain bucket shapes. Pause additional rollouts until fairness metrics validated.
- Auth sidecar token caching — PR #412 merged to staging; plan: staged rollout to canary region with synthetic cert rotations.
- Route affinity tweak (hotfix) — small change deployed to 4 clusters; needs verification during next 48h to ensure no imbalance in route hot-spotting.

Decisions made this sync:
- Do not expand allocator experiment beyond 3% until next checkpoint (owner: Diego).
- Revert quota heuristic for low-tier users in 2 non-critical clusters now; schedule proper refactor for next sprint (owner: Sana).
- Auth cert rotation policy: introduce a staggered sidecar refresh with backoff for 3 rotations; implement canary simulation for rotations (owner: Liam).

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya: Draft postmortem skeleton for KV cache miss incident and route to SRE for review — due 2027-08-06.
- Diego: Add instrumentation to rehydration workers (queue depth + time-to-hotload) and ship to staging — due 2027-08-09.
- Sana: Create Linear tickets to revert and then refactor quota heuristic + add unit test cases for starvation — due 2027-08-05.
- Liam: Prepare canary job to simulate cert rotation sidecar load and wire into CI — due 2027-08-10.
- Priya (SRE): Coordinate a post-deploy smoke pass for auth caching change and record results in runbook — due 2027-08-07.
- Ezra: Pause allocator rollout, capture more tail latencies, and aggregate per-model shape histograms — due 2027-08-06.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Is the current cache invalidation model (synchronous tombstone + async rehydrate) fundamentally brittle under sustained concurrent writes? Options: stronger locking, epoch-based invalidation, or a move to multi-version cache. (Spike recommended)
- Quota fairness: do we add per-tenant minimum baseline tokens or tune eviction windows? Need product input on minimum guaranteed throughput for low-tier customers.
- Should cert rotations always be staggered by region? Sidecars globally do refresh too fast and we lack a global throttle.

Notes / references:
- See linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/412 (auth refresh throttle)
- Linear: PLT-4123 allocator imbalance notes + synthetic harness link
- Slack thread recap: #platform-routing — summarised in pinned message on 2027-08-04

Quick wins (to consider this sprint):
- Add a tiny jitter to sidecar refresh windows to prevent synchronized storms. (quick patch)
- Add a cache-rehydrate queue depth alert to the platform observability stack (pager threshold low)
- Add a synthetic daily cert rotation job in staging that simulates 200k sidecars refreshes to validate behaviour

Closing notes:
- No customer-facing outages but operationally noisy. Prioritise invariant fixes and better synthetic coverage for rotations + cache rehydrates. Next sync: 2027-08-11 09:00 UTC (same time).

Raw scribbles / scratch (notes to self):
- debug trace id examples: trace: cplane-20270804-9f3b
- check region e2 for steady-state high rehydrate queue (alerts spinning in Grafana)
- follow up with product on baseline quota guarantees (cc @karen-p)
